cywordle.clue: Computer Emergency Response Team — the coordination group you notify when an ICS incident hits.
The fix a vendor ships for a known vulnerability — applying it in OT usually needs a planned maintenance window.
A widely used PLC programming language whose diagrams resemble the rails and rungs of this physical structure.
The highest-privilege account on a Unix-based system, and often an attacker's ultimate goal after breaching a network.
Malware built to permanently destroy or erase data and systems rather than steal it — used in some of the most destructive attacks on OT networks.
An outdated system or piece of equipment still running well past its expected lifespan, common in OT environments and often hard to patch or secure.
A fixed-size digital fingerprint of a file or message, used to confirm it has not been altered or tampered with.
A server that sits between an OT network zone and other systems, relaying and inspecting traffic on its behalf rather than allowing direct connections.
A widely used industrial communication protocol connecting PLCs, sensors, and control devices.
An electrically operated switch that uses a small control signal to open or close a circuit controlling much larger OT equipment.
An incident where an attacker gains unauthorized access to a network or system.
A device that measures physical conditions like temperature or pressure and reports them to controllers.
A hierarchical reference model that segments industrial networks into levels, separating OT control systems from the corporate IT network.
In IEC 62443, the secure communication pathway connecting one zone of an industrial network to another.
A device that translates between protocols, often bridging OT and IT networks or connecting legacy equipment to modern systems.
A network deliberately isolated with no physical or wireless connection to other networks, used to protect critical OT systems.
Malware that hides inside a system to give an attacker persistent, hard-to-detect access.
Deliberately altering a device or its readings without authorization — a key OT/ICS security concern.
A malware's periodic signal back to its command-and-control server, revealing a hidden compromise.
